circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281-kilometre track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support series events and holding FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km motorsport venue that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate periods. Originally constructed as the Österreichring, it held the race annually from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing modifications and rebranding as the A1-Ring, during which it again staged the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city situated along the waterfront boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. Formula One racing began here with the 2016 European Grand Prix, followed by the establishment of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as the circuit's primary annual event from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1 licensed track has accommodated various motorsport categories, including GP2 Series, Australian V8 Supercars (2006-2010), and 24-hour endurance competitions, with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner types, making it a comprehensive test of driver and car capabilities. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Ardennes region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7-kilometre circuit has been a staple of motorsport since hosting the Belgian Grand Prix in 1925. The venue became part of Formula One's inaugural 1950 season and has continuously held the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only brief interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various other motorsport competitions including international sportscar racing and North American series events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events since 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, positioned in Northamptonshire, England, serves as the traditional venue for the British Grand Prix since inaugurating the event in 1948. The circuit gained additional significance as the location of the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the British Grand Prix subsequently alternated between three venues before returning to Silverstone as its permanent home from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km track near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix in the Eastern Bloc when racing commenced there in 1986, just eight months after construction began. Originally intended as a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the project was relocated to a countryside site near a major highway by the Hungarian government, resulting in the fastest-built Formula One venue at that time.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, missing only the 1980 season for renovation, making it one of just four circuits to feature continuously on the Formula One calendar from its inception, and it earned the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its distinctive long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometres and holds up to 155,000 spectators. Operated by Honda Mobilityland, the track is renowned for hosting prestigious Formula One races alongside Japanese Super Formula competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving past the city's most iconic hospitality venues and landmarks along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout incorporates famous casino resorts and entertainment attractions, creating a track that mirrors the distinctive geography of the renowned entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring racing brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, having previously held the race on a different configuration until 1992, and now presents the event as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami's temporary street circuit wraps around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since welcomed electric racing from 2025 onwards using a modified configuration.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, circling the local harbour. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, the circuit is universally known as Monte Carlo due to its primary location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted Formula One's Dutch Grand Prix after its return to the calendar in 2021. The venue's tenure in the sport concluded in 2026, ending a brief but significant chapter in the circuit's modern racing history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motorsport venue situated near Doha, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate deceased Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and houses a karting facility dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend, Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021, while also hosting electric racing competition from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang zones into its route layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its viewing areas.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track also hosts major international racing series including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the FIA World Endurance Championship, making it one of North America's premier motorsport destinations.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two World Championships won with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 career race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including consecutive Le Mans 24 Hours wins with Toyota and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to claim titles in both Formula One and World Endurance competition.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes in 2025 and has already secured eight victories on the Formula One circuit.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, representing his nation in the sport's premier motorsport series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, bringing his competitive driving skills to the sport's premier championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 13 seasons and 10 race victories to the team. He achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during 2019 and 2020 while competing for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto, an Argentine driver, currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's top category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has appeared in seven Formula One races between 2024 and 2025 while serving as a reserve for Haas. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, holding dual French and Algerian nationality, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024 before transitioning to other racing disciplines. He currently competes as a BMW factory driver in the World Endurance Championship with WRT while also competing part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship after competing in the sport for eight seasons. Across his career in the championship, he has secured victories in 13 Grand Prix races.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One with Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory in 2021 at the Hungarian round while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican driver competing in Formula One for Cadillac who finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while at Red Bull. Over his 15-year career in the sport, he has claimed six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren who has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell represents Britain in Formula One as a driver for Mercedes, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having transitioned from endurance racing with Era Motorsports in IMSA's LMP2 class. His Formula One career spanned 2023 to 2024 before moving to international sports car competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds reserve status with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen represents Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, Verstappen has accumulated 72 Grand Prix victories, establishing himself as one of the sport's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac team in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated under the Alpine name from 2021 onwards as Renault's factory squad, following a rebranding from its previous Renault F1 Team identity to highlight the luxury sports car marque. Alpine maintained this works team status until Renault's departure from the sport concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through multiple team configurations, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team name.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished team, participating in every World Championship since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially referred to by their emblem's equine nickname, represents the longest continuous presence and greatest success record in the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American team owner Gene Haas launched this Formula One outfit in 2014, with operations commencing in the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had led the team since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport engineering firm established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, the team initially excelled in endurance racing before transitioning to Formula One in 1993. Operating as an independent constructor, it competed in the sport for over three decades until departing in 2025 as one of the four longest-serving teams by race entries. Audi AG acquired the company and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own Formula One venture.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing, based in Woking, England, is a British Formula One outfit competing under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group and is wholly owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the modern team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas operation became a three-way partnership in 2022 when Ineos joined alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The team's heritage is synonymous with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as part of the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation within the Red Bull motorsports structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two premier-class entries controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the managerial role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Operating from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the team has maintained a significant presence in the sport as both competitor and car manufacturer for nearly five decades.
